posts.title: The History of Khinkali in Georgia
posts.excerpt: Khinkali, Georgia's iconic soup dumpling, traces its roots to the mountain regions of Khevsureti and Pshavi, where shepherds needed a hearty, portable meal. At BiteClub, we still hand-fold every khinkali the traditional way, using a recipe passed down through generations.
body: Khinkali first appeared in the highlands of eastern Georgia — Khevsureti, Pshavi and Tusheti — sometime in the 7th or 8th century. Shepherds and warriors needed a filling, easy-to-carry meal that could survive long days in the mountains, and the soup-filled dumpling was the answer: simple ingredients, sealed inside a thick dough wrapper twisted into a topknot.

Over the centuries the recipe spread down from the mountains into the valleys and cities, picking up regional variations along the way. Some regions favor a peppery beef and pork filling, others prefer pure lamb, and in summer, cheese or mushroom khinkali became popular meat-free alternatives.

At BiteClub, we honor that mountain tradition. Every khinkali on our menu is hand-folded to order, filled with a well-seasoned meat mixture and a spoonful of rich broth that bursts with the first bite. We serve them the traditional way too — no fork required, just your hands, a generous dusting of black pepper, and plenty of napkins.
posts.pullQuote: A proper khinkali should never be cut with a knife — pick it up by the topknot, take a bite, and let the broth do the talking.
posts.closingParagraph: Whether you're trying khinkali for the first time or you grew up eating them at your grandmother's table, we hope our version brings a little bit of the Georgian mountains to your plate.

comments.name: Nino
comments.text: This is exactly how my grandmother described khinkali from Khevsureti. Loved the history!

comments.name: Levan
comments.text: Tried the khinkali here last week — the broth was perfect. Great article too.

posts.title: Our New Spring Menu
posts.excerpt: Spring has arrived and so has a refreshed BiteClub menu, built around the season's first greens, herbs and vegetables. From a bright new chakapuli to a lighter lobio, here's what's new on the table.
body: Every spring, our kitchen team starts planning the new menu around what's actually growing — fresh tarragon, young garlic, spring onions, and the first tender greens from local farms around Tbilisi. This year is no different, and we've built a handful of new dishes entirely around those ingredients.

The star of the new menu is our Chakapuli, made with lamb, plenty of fresh tarragon, green plums and white wine — a dish that traditionally marks the start of spring in Georgian homes. We've also lightened up our Lobio, adding fresh herbs and a touch of walnut for extra depth without the heaviness of a winter stew.

For something cooler, try our new seasonal salad with young greens, radish and a simple sour-plum dressing — it pairs perfectly with warm mchadi straight from the pan. As always, everything is made fresh daily, so the menu will keep evolving as the season goes on.
posts.pullQuote: Spring in Georgia has a flavor of its own — tarragon, green garlic and the first sour plums of the year. We wanted our new menu to taste like exactly that.
posts.closingParagraph: Come try the new dishes while the season lasts — we'll be rotating a few items out as summer produce starts to arrive.

comments.name: Mariam
comments.text: The new chakapuli is amazing, so fresh and full of tarragon flavor.

comments.name: David
comments.text: Loved the lighter lobio, perfect for spring. Can't wait to try more new dishes.

posts.title: 5 Reasons to Visit BiteClub This Weekend
posts.excerpt: Looking for a place to relax this weekend? From our weekend specials to live music nights, here are five reasons to grab a table at BiteClub before Sunday.
body: 1. Weekend specials. Every Saturday and Sunday we put a couple of limited dishes on the menu that you won't find during the week — think slow-cooked stews and seasonal specials our chefs have been testing all week. 2. A relaxed atmosphere. Our dining room and terrace are built for lingering — good for a long lunch with friends or a slow dinner that turns into dessert and coffee.

3. Fresh, local ingredients. We work with farms around Tbilisi to source vegetables, herbs and dairy, so what's on your plate changes a little with the seasons — and it always tastes like it was made that morning. 4. Something for everyone at the table. Whether someone wants classic khinkali, a lighter salad, or a proper Georgian feast, our menu covers enough ground that nobody has to compromise.

5. It's the perfect reset before Monday. A good meal, a comfortable seat, and no rush to leave — sometimes that's exactly what a weekend is for. Bring your family, your friends, or just come alone with a book; we'll take care of the rest.
posts.pullQuote: The best weekends start with a table, good food, and no reason to check the time.
posts.closingParagraph: We'd love to see you this weekend — no need for a special occasion, just come hungry.

comments.name: Ana
comments.text: Went this weekend and the atmosphere was exactly as described — will be back.

comments.name: Giorgi
comments.text: Great list, the weekend specials convinced me to book a table.
